case_identity.title: The Nannup Four
case_identity.summary: Four people — Simon Kadwill (real name Gary Felton/Simon Cook), his partner Chantelle McDougall, their 5-year-old daughter Leela, and friend Tony Popic — vanished from a farmhouse in a tiny town. Kadwill led a fringe doomsday belief system, used a stolen identity, and the group left behind dogs, clothes, and a partly eaten dinner. A coronial inquest left open whether it was cult murder-suicide or an engineered disappearance.

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: From November 2003, Chantelle Jane McDougall, Gary Felton, also known as Simon Anthony Kadwill, and their daughter Leela McDougall lived on a rented rural property in Nannup; their friend Antonio Konstantin Popic resided with them intermittently in a caravan.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: Gary Felton was also known as Simon Anthony Kadwill and was described in the coronial finding as a British national and a self-styled spiritual leader.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: In about May 2006, Simon, Chantelle and Tony began telling family and friends that they intended to move to Brazil.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: On 10 July 2007, Tony sold his vehicle to a dealer in Bridgetown; the next day or so, he visited his parents in Manjimup and said goodbye to them.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: On 13 July 2007, Chantelle sold her car to a car dealer in Busselton and sold three of her dog's puppies to a pet shop there; on 14 July 2007, she sold the remaining puppy and the adult dogs to Carolyn French, who drove to Nannup to buy them.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: On 16 July 2007, the owners of the rural property found the house vacated in spotless condition, with several valuable furnishings left behind, and found a note from Chantelle indicating that the group had gone to Brazil.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: The note left at the property said that the group had left suddenly because of lack of sleep created by electromagnetic fields and had moved overseas to Brazil.
verified_facts.speaker: Chantelle McDougall, Gary Felton, Antonio Konstantin Popic and Leela McDougall

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: In October 2007, Chantelle's father reported to police in Victoria that Chantelle and Leela were missing and that he had serious concerns for their welfare; Tony's brother contacted Western Australian Police in early November 2007 to report Tony missing.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: A Western Australia Police missing-persons investigation led by First Class Constable Lucy Greatorex resulted in 444 investigative actions, but the group's movements and whereabouts were not established.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: On 29 December 2016, the State Coroner determined that there was reasonable cause to suspect that the group had died and directed that the suspected deaths be investigated.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: Coroner Barry Paul King held an inquest into the suspected deaths at Busselton Courthouse from 6 to 8 December 2017.
verified_facts.speaker: Barry Paul King

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: The coroner found that the death of none of the four had been established beyond reasonable doubt and clarified that this did not mean that any member of the group had been found alive.
verified_facts.speaker: Barry Paul King

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996
‘Impossible’ to tell if Nannup cult family still alive

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: On 31 October 2007, police attended a remote bush location near Northcliffe after prison workers reportedly found a woman's old red T-shirt and reported smelling dead flesh; police seized the T-shirt, but the coronial finding records no forensic examination of it and no recorded search of the bushland at that time.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: Police later could not locate the T-shirt seized near Northcliffe, and the coronial finding states that investigators did not follow up that and other reports during the original investigation, resulting in lost investigative opportunities.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: A full forensic examination was not conducted of the group's house and caravan after the missing-persons report; a later search in April 2008 also did not include a full forensic examination because time had passed and new tenants occupied the property.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: On 12 and 13 January 2015, a Western Australia Police dive squad searched the five dams on the property that had existed in 2007; the search revealed no evidence of the group.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: On 15 July 2007, Tony's mobile phone was used in Northbridge, a man identified as Tony received a pizza in King's Park, and a person using Tony's driver's licence checked into the Underground Backpackers Hostel; the coroner considered it highly likely that Tony had traveled to Perth that day.
verified_facts.speaker: Barry Paul King

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: No confirmed evidence of contact or sighting of any member of the group was established after their disappearance.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: Investigators found no recorded activity by the group with a range of agencies after the disappearance, including passport, banking, government-support, utilities, airline, bus and accommodation records.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

verified_facts.canonical_claim_en: Western Australia Police confirmed that a previous search near Northcliffe had been conducted in the wrong area because the search coordinates were based on an officer's memory and the original location had not been officially recorded.

Chantelle McDougall, her daughter Leela, Simon Kadwill and Tony Popic vanished from the outskirts of the small West Australian town in 2007. timeline.canonical_claim_en: From November 2003, Chantelle Jane McDougall, Gary Felton, also known as Simon Anthony Kadwill, and their daughter Leela McDougall lived on a rented rural property in Nannup; their friend Antonio Konstantin Popic resided with them intermittently in a caravan.

timeline.canonical_claim_en: In about May 2006, Simon, Chantelle and Tony began telling family and friends that they intended to move to Brazil.

timeline.canonical_claim_en: In May 2007, Simon told an online follower that the group had a plan for a family suicide involving a quick-acting drug and walking into a wilderness area; the account was reported to the inquest through the follower's evidence.
timeline.speaker: Gary Felton / Simon Anthony Kadwill

timeline.canonical_claim_en: Investigators found no recorded activity by the group with a range of agencies after the disappearance, including passport, banking, government-support, utilities, airline, bus and accommodation records.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

timeline.canonical_claim_en: On 10 July 2007, Tony sold his vehicle to a dealer in Bridgetown; the next day or so, he visited his parents in Manjimup and said goodbye to them.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

timeline.canonical_claim_en: On 13 July 2007, Chantelle sold her car to a car dealer in Busselton and sold three of her dog's puppies to a pet shop there; on 14 July 2007, she sold the remaining puppy and the adult dogs to Carolyn French, who drove to Nannup to buy them.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

timeline.canonical_claim_en: On 15 and 16 July 2007, tickets were purchased under the name J Roberts or J Robwerts for travel involving Perth, Northcliffe and Kalgoorlie; adult male passengers undertook the Northcliffe and Kalgoorlie journeys, but the identities of the travelers were not established.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

timeline.canonical_claim_en: On 15 July 2007, Tony's mobile phone was used in Northbridge, a man identified as Tony received a pizza in King's Park, and a person using Tony's driver's licence checked into the Underground Backpackers Hostel; the coroner considered it highly likely that Tony had traveled to Perth that day.
timeline.speaker: Barry Paul King

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

timeline.canonical_claim_en: On 16 July 2007, the owners of the rural property found the house vacated in spotless condition, with several valuable furnishings left behind, and found a note from Chantelle indicating that the group had gone to Brazil.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

timeline.canonical_claim_en: The note left at the property said that the group had left suddenly because of lack of sleep created by electromagnetic fields and had moved overseas to Brazil.
timeline.speaker: Chantelle McDougall, Gary Felton, Antonio Konstantin Popic and Leela McDougall

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

timeline.canonical_claim_en: In October 2007, Chantelle's father reported to police in Victoria that Chantelle and Leela were missing and that he had serious concerns for their welfare; Tony's brother contacted Western Australian Police in early November 2007 to report Tony missing.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

timeline.canonical_claim_en: A full forensic examination was not conducted of the group's house and caravan after the missing-persons report; a later search in April 2008 also did not include a full forensic examination because time had passed and new tenants occupied the property.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

timeline.canonical_claim_en: On 31 October 2007, police attended a remote bush location near Northcliffe after prison workers reportedly found a woman's old red T-shirt and reported smelling dead flesh; police seized the T-shirt, but the coronial finding records no forensic examination of it and no recorded search of the bushland at that time.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

timeline.canonical_claim_en: Police later could not locate the T-shirt seized near Northcliffe, and the coronial finding states that investigators did not follow up that and other reports during the original investigation, resulting in lost investigative opportunities.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

timeline.canonical_claim_en: On 12 and 13 January 2015, a Western Australia Police dive squad searched the five dams on the property that had existed in 2007; the search revealed no evidence of the group.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

timeline.canonical_claim_en: On 29 December 2016, the State Coroner determined that there was reasonable cause to suspect that the group had died and directed that the suspected deaths be investigated.

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

timeline.canonical_claim_en: Coroner Barry Paul King held an inquest into the suspected deaths at Busselton Courthouse from 6 to 8 December 2017.
timeline.speaker: Barry Paul King

source_refs.title: Coroners Act, 1996
Coroners Act, 1996

timeline.canonical_claim_en: The coroner found that the death of none of the four had been established beyond reasonable doubt and clarified that this did not mean that any member of the group had been found alive.
timeline.speaker: Barry Paul King

timeline.canonical_claim_en: The coroner identified evidence supporting both the possibility that the group was dead and the contrary possibility that they were alive and living in seclusion after orchestrating their disappearance.
